# Red-on-Rust — Controlled Specification-Processing Pipeline

**DERIVED POINTER — generated by the controlled specification pipeline. Not a normative source.** The authority for anything summarized here is named in the same row; where a projection and an authority differ, the authority governs and `scripts/spec/_gate.py` fails.

*generated by `redonrust-spec-pipeline` v`1.0.0` · stage `PUB` · seed source `Red-on-Rust.md` @ `sha256:2aeb9940665f6ef27bbba9895889e93b8be8c1ba9f5ff0558f2b95fee07a25eb` · render `sha256:06a56825de98e4fc…`*

**Version 1.0 · mode: specification-processing infrastructure only · M0: `NOT STARTED` · no Rust implementation, no runtime, no test harness (§21).**

The repository's executable contract for transforming its own specification. The LLM — and this generator — is a proposal engine inside a deterministic governance machine: it may propose, it may not authorize (§23).

## 1. Pipeline

```
RAW SEED SOURCE  Red-on-Rust.md
  ↓ S0 SNAPSHOT      identity + provenance      -> source.sha256, snapshot.json
  ↓ S1 EXTRACT       requirement/obligation candidates, normative class, proposals.json
  ↓ S2 SPLIT         sections (lossless, spec/02 order)
  ↓ S3 NORMALIZE     terminology / predicate / identifier registration (no rewriting)
  ↓ S4 AUDIT         16 categories · findings projected · integrity scans
  ↓ S5 CANONICALIZE  reconstruction ⊆ NormativeContent(spec/01)
  ↓ S6 REGISTER      requirements · obligations · terminology · dependencies
  ↓ S6b VECTORS      registered fixtures (canonical / persistence / effects)
  ↓ S7 VERIFY        cross-artifact battery over every projection (§14)
```

Authority distinction preserved end to end: `SOURCE ≠ PROPOSAL ≠ DERIVED ARTIFACT ≠ CANONICAL AUTHORITY`.

## 2. Entry points

```
python3 scripts/spec/pipeline.py Red-on-Rust.md          # full pipeline -> build/spec/
python3 scripts/spec/pipeline.py Red-on-Rust.md --check  # prove the build set is current
python3 scripts/spec/pipeline.py --verify-only           # render + S7 battery, write nothing
python3 scripts/spec/pipeline.py --list                  # stages and their contracts
python3 scripts/spec/pipeline.py --report                # the §24 transformation report
python3 scripts/spec/pipeline.py --publish-derived       # rewrite spec/0*-*/ + PIPELINE.md
python3 scripts/spec/pipeline.py --strict                  # refuse to canonicalize over open BLOCKING/MAJOR
python3 scripts/spec/_gate.py --strict                     # the same refusal, as a gate proof
python3 scripts/spec/_gate.py                            # the repository gate (check.py)
python3 tests/spec/_pipeline_mutations.py                # drift-detection battery
```

Stage flags (`--snapshot … --verify`, `--all`) select which stage summaries are printed; every run executes the full ordered pipeline, because a stage that could run alone would be a stage whose failure the others could not see (§19).

## 3. Trust model (§3, §17)

```
LLM -> proposes extraction / splitting / normalization / terminology / dependencies /
      ambiguities  ->  deterministic validators -> PASS: accepted artifact
                                              -> FAIL: audit + review
```

This pipeline never: defines canonical authority; invents, deletes, merges, splits, renumbers or re-predicates a requirement; alters a historical record; overwrites a canonical artifact without validation; or claims verification because something was generated. `Canonicalize(X) ⊆ NormativeContent(X)` is enforced by chunk-multiset equality (current render: EQUAL).

## 4. Invariants honoured (§4)

| invariant | mechanism | failure behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| provenance | every artifact names source hash, path, pipeline version, stage, generator and inputs; every registry row names where its value was copied from | missing provenance → S7 fails |
| determinism | no clock, no randomness, no locale, no network, no directory order; sorted rendering; JSON `sort_keys`; registry order for lists | S7 scans the stage sources and fails on an offender |
| idempotence | `Pipeline(Pipeline(X)) == Pipeline(X)` on canonical content — the reconstruction is chunk-identical to `spec/01`; publishing compares bytes before writing | multiset inequality → S5 refuses |
| no normative invention | generators read registers only; every published cell names its authority | unregistered identity → S7 fails |
| identity preservation | `spec/03`'s ID set *and order* are the output's ID set and order | divergence → S7 fails |
| timestamps | absent from semantic content and from every canonical hash (§4.1) | a `timestamp_present: true` field would fail the schema |

Reproducibility is proven by `render_hash`, a content address over the whole artifact set (`build/spec/manifest.json`).

## 5. Fail-closed (§19)

Any stage failure aborts before a byte is written; verification failure means the canonical state is not accepted. A failed audit blocks canonicalization under `--strict`; under the default policy unresolved rows are carried **and disclosed** in the canonical artifact's open-items section, because dropping them would be the fabricated completeness §16 prohibits and `spec/01` itself publishes them as open.

## 6. Relationship to existing governance (§20)

| existing artifact | relation |
|---|---|
| `Red-on-Rust.md` | S0 input; read-only, hash-pinned |
| `spec/01` / `spec/02` / `spec/03` | normative text, section and registry authorities for S1/S2/S5/S6 |
| `spec/06` / `spec/09` / `req/03` | finding, decision and ambiguity registers projected by S4 (never re-graded) |
| `req/` (545 atomic) | atomic layer of `build/spec/obligations.json` |
| `mod/` / `dep/` / `term/` | ownership, dependency and terminology authorities (projected, not copied) |
| `audit/` | 12 sha256-pinned historical snapshots, re-verified untouched by S7 |
| `final/` / `reg/` / `state/` | compiled and canonical projections cross-checked by S1/S7 |
| `check.py` | `scripts/spec/_gate.py` is registered as one more checker, so this pipeline is gated by the same rule as every other organization |

No identity in any of the above is renamed, renumbered or re-graded by this pipeline, and no new identifier namespace is added to a register: pipeline-local ids (`VEC-…`) exist only inside derived build artifacts and are declared additive there.

## 7. Pre-M0 boundary (§21)

Forbidden and absent: Rust runtime, CEK, capability kernel, actor, scheduler, host, persistence, effect and agent implementations. Proof is mechanical rather than aspirational: S7 walks the tree and fails if any `*.rs` file or `Cargo.toml` exists (a gate cannot prevent a file from being written, but no run whose tree contains one is green). A pipeline run writes only under `build/spec/` (gitignored, reproducible), the committed pointers, `spec/PIPELINE.md` and `TRANSFORMATION-REPORT.md`; the seed source is opened read-only and every write compares bytes first, so a run with nothing to publish publishes nothing.

## 8. Evidence discipline (§22's last boxes)

Verification PASS proves agreement between projections and authorities — repository-integrity evidence only. It does not promote a status, does not verify an obligation, does not lift `REF1-CONDITIONAL` or `V1-CONDITIONAL`, and does not start M0.
